Diagnostics and Assertions for Periods

Source: R/period_diagnose.R
period_diagnose_levels.Rd

Check whether period labels meet conditions. The diagnose functions report on each condition, and the assert functions throw an error if a condition is not met.

  • period_diagnose_values() and period_assert_values() check the elements of labels.

  • period_diagnose_levels() and period_assert_levels() check the levels of labels, including any unused levels. Both functions require labels to be a factor.

Conditions include:

  • Not overlapping

  • Not having gaps

  • Not having totals or missing values

  • Having, or not having, open periods

Usage

period_diagnose_levels(
  labels,
  no_overlap = FALSE,
  no_gap = FALSE,
  no_total = FALSE,
  no_missing = FALSE,
  no_open_left = FALSE,
  no_open_right = FALSE,
  has_open_left = FALSE,
  has_open_right = FALSE,
  interpret_single = c("lower", "upper"),
  interpret_multi = NULL,
  interpret_fail = c("error", "warn", "silent")
)

period_assert_levels(
  labels,
  no_overlap = FALSE,
  no_gap = FALSE,
  no_total = FALSE,
  no_missing = FALSE,
  no_open_left = FALSE,
  no_open_right = FALSE,
  has_open_left = FALSE,
  has_open_right = FALSE,
  interpret_single = c("lower", "upper"),
  interpret_multi = NULL,
  interpret_fail = c("error", "warn", "silent")
)

period_diagnose_values(
  labels,
  no_overlap = FALSE,
  no_gap = FALSE,
  no_total = FALSE,
  no_missing = FALSE,
  no_open_left = FALSE,
  no_open_right = FALSE,
  has_open_left = FALSE,
  has_open_right = FALSE,
  interpret_single = c("lower", "upper"),
  interpret_multi = NULL,
  interpret_fail = c("error", "warn", "silent")
)

period_assert_values(
  labels,
  no_overlap = FALSE,
  no_gap = FALSE,
  no_total = FALSE,
  no_missing = FALSE,
  no_open_left = FALSE,
  no_open_right = FALSE,
  has_open_left = FALSE,
  has_open_right = FALSE,
  interpret_single = c("lower", "upper"),
  interpret_multi = NULL,
  interpret_fail = c("error", "warn", "silent")
)

Arguments

labels

Vector of period labels.

no_overlap

Check that no periods overlap. Different labels that describe the same interval, such as "2020-2025" and "2020 to 2025", count as overlapping. Totals and missing values, as defined by period_is_total() and period_is_missing(), are removed before checks for overlaps are performed. Default is FALSE (don't check).

no_gap

Check that all periods between the earliest and latest periods are included. Default is FALSE (don't check).

no_total

Check that there is no "total" category, as defined by period_is_total(). Default is FALSE (don't check).

no_missing

Check that there is no "missing" category, as defined by period_is_missing(). Default is FALSE (don't check).

no_open_left

Check that no period is open on the left (has no lower limit), as defined by period_is_open_left(). Default is FALSE (don't check).

no_open_right

Check that no period is open on the right (has no upper limit), as defined by period_is_open_right(). Default is FALSE (don't check).

has_open_left

Check that at least one period is open on the left (has no lower limit), as defined by period_is_open_left(). Default is FALSE (don't check).

has_open_right

Check that at least one period is open on the right (has no upper limit), as defined by period_is_open_right(). Default is FALSE (don't check).

interpret_single

How to interpret a label for a single year, such as "2020". Choices are "lower" (the default) and "upper". See below for details.

interpret_multi

How to interpret a label that refers to multiple years, such as "2020-2025". Choices are NULL (the default), "at_upper", and "below_upper". See below for details.

interpret_fail

Action if element of labels cannot be interpreted. Choices are "error" (the default), "warn", and "silent".

Value

  • period_diagnose_levels() and period_diagnose_values() return a list with a logical flag called ok and a tibble called details.

  • period_assert_levels() and period_assert_values() return labels invisibly, or raise an error.

Rules for interpreting inputs

Single-year

Labels for single-year periods sometimes refer to the lower limits of periods, and sometimes refer to upper limits. For instance, the label "2020" is sometimes used to refer to the period that starts at midnight on 1 January 2020 and ends at midnight on 1 January 2021, and is sometimes used to refer to the period that starts at midnight on 1 July 2019 and ends at midnight on 1 July 2020.

The interpret_single argument can be used to distinguish between the two conventions:

interpret_singleRuleExample
"lower""a" -> [a,a+1)"2020" -> [2020,2021)
"upper""a" -> [a-1,a)"2020" -> [2019,2020)

Multi-year

In labels for multi-year periods, the second number is sometimes the upper limit of the period, and sometimes the upper limit minus 1. For instance, the period that starts at midnight on 1 January 2020 and ends at midnight on 1 January 2025 is sometimes labelled "2020-2025" and is sometimes labelled "2020-2024".

The interpret_multi argument can be used to distinguish between the two conventions:

interpret_multiRuleExample
"at_upper""a-b" -> [a,b)"2020-2025" -> [2020,2025)
"below_upper""a-b" -> [a,b+1)"2020-2024" -> [2020,2025)

If interpret_multi is NULL (the default), then multi-year labels are interpreted using the "at_upper" convention. If, however, the "at_upper" convention leads to intervals with widths 4, 9, 14, ..., then agetime emits a message. Supplying an explicit value for interpret_multi silences this message.

Open

A period that is open on the left has no lower limit, and a period that is open on the right has no upper limit. Labels for open periods are not affected by interpret_single or interpret_multi.

Some examples of open periods:

LabelInterval
"<2000", "before 2000", "under 2000"(-Inf,2000)
"2000 or earlier", "up to 2000"(-Inf,2001)
"2000+", "2000 or more", "2000 or later"[2000,Inf)

Labels starting with "-", such as "-2000", are not accepted.

See also

  • age_assert_values(), age_assert_levels()

  • age_diagnose_values(), age_diagnose_levels()

  • cohort_assert_values(), cohort_assert_levels()

  • cohort_diagnose_values(), cohort_diagnose_levels()

Examples

lab <- period_labels_five(
  lower_first = 2020,
  lower_last = 2030
)
lab
#> [1] "2020-2025" "2025-2030" "2030-2035"

## get info on everything
period_diagnose_values(
  labels = lab,
  no_overlap = TRUE,
  no_gap = TRUE,
  no_total = TRUE,
  no_missing = TRUE
)
#> $ok
#> [1] TRUE
#> 
#> $details
#> # A tibble: 4 × 3
#>   condition  passed comment
#>   <chr>      <lgl>  <chr>  
#> 1 no_overlap TRUE   NA     
#> 2 no_gap     TRUE   NA     
#> 3 no_total   TRUE   NA     
#> 4 no_missing TRUE   NA     
#> 

## throw error if overlap or gap
period_assert_values(
  labels = lab,
  no_overlap = TRUE,
  no_gap = TRUE
)

## repeated labels count as overlapping...
df <- data.frame(
  period = c("2020-2025", "2025-2030", "2020-2025", "2025-2030"),
  sex = c("F", "F", "M", "M")
)
period_diagnose_values(df$period, no_overlap = TRUE)
#> $ok
#> [1] FALSE
#> 
#> $details
#> # A tibble: 1 × 3
#>   condition  passed comment                                                     
#>   <chr>      <lgl>  <chr>                                                       
#> 1 no_overlap FALSE  Example of overlap among values: '2020-2025' appears 2 time…
#> 

## ...so check within groups
library(dplyr, warn.conflicts = FALSE)
df |>
  group_by(sex) |>
  mutate(period = period_assert_values(period, no_overlap = TRUE))
#> # A tibble: 4 × 2
#> # Groups:   sex [2]
#>   period    sex  
#>   <chr>     <chr>
#> 1 2020-2025 F    
#> 2 2025-2030 F    
#> 3 2020-2025 M    
#> 4 2025-2030 M    

## factor with unused level
fac <- factor(
  x = "2020-2025",
  levels = c("2020-2025", "2030-2035")
)
fac
#> [1] 2020-2025
#> Levels: 2020-2025 2030-2035
period_diagnose_levels(fac, no_gap = TRUE)
#> $ok
#> [1] FALSE
#> 
#> $details
#> # A tibble: 1 × 3
#>   condition passed comment                                    
#>   <chr>     <lgl>  <chr>                                      
#> 1 no_gap    FALSE  Example: gap among levels below '2030-2035'
#> 
period_diagnose_values(fac, no_gap = TRUE)
#> $ok
#> [1] TRUE
#> 
#> $details
#> # A tibble: 1 × 3
#>   condition passed comment
#>   <chr>     <lgl>  <chr>  
#> 1 no_gap    TRUE   NA     
#>
